title: 他与她的梦 6他与她的梦 5
lines: 精神病院走廊深处慢慢传来歌声。
那声音很老，像是某种留声机里放出来的旧唱片，带着沙沙的杂音，音调忽高忽低，偶尔走调，却又带着一种诡异的、让人忍不住想去听的旋律。人声有些低沉，歌词听不清，只能隐约辨认出几个零碎的词。
格林没有在意，他只是在走廊里走着，推开一扇又一扇门。那些门上的数字编号已经模糊了，有的房间是空的，只有一张倾倒的床和积满灰尘的地板。
有的房间里堆满了旧病历，纸张泛黄，上面的字迹像是某种已经失传的文字，没法阅读；
还有的房间门口被什么东西堵住了——像是某种巨大的、黑色的块状物，堵得严严实实。
格林没有强行推开那些，他只是继续走。
拐过一道弯后，他停在了一扇门前面，这个和其他的有点不太一样。
格林推开那扇门，房间很小。里面的墙上装着一样东西——一个拉杆。黄铜色的，握柄处已经磨得发亮，像是被很多人拉过。
格林走过去，低头看了看那个拉杆。能感觉到拉杆底座连接着某种魔法回路，那些回路像树根一样延伸进墙壁和地板里，通向整栋建筑的各个角落。
“似乎会改变一些房间结构，但是能够让真正的路显现出来。”
格林仔细看了看那些回路的走向。它们错综复杂，但并没有形成闭合的回路——也就是说，不是陷阱。
至少不是那种会直接把房间里的人炸成碎片的陷阱，对于格林来说，哪怕爆炸也无所谓，可要是爱丽丝的线索消失了就糟糕了。
格林握住拉杆，往下一拉。
“咔嗒。”
灯光瞬间熄灭。
同时，房间外面的走廊里，响起了一阵急促的脚步声——又像是摩擦声，像是很多双鞋底在粗糙的地面上快速移动。
格林松开拉杆，转身面向门口。
然后那些人影涌了进来，巨大的黑色人影，比正常人类高出半截身子。它们穿着白色的护士服，但那白色已经泛黄，上面沾着暗色的污渍。
它们的手里拿着针管——不是普通的针管，那些针管足有手臂那么长，针尖在黑暗中泛着不祥的光。脸是黑的，什么都没有，和之前的行人怪物还不一样。
格林动了。
他没有武器——那把断剑在进入精神病院之前就已经彻底报废了。但格林现在也不需要武器，他的手就是武器。
第一只护士怪物冲过来，针管直刺他的胸口。
格林侧身，左手抓住那只握着针管的手腕，用力一拧。咔嚓。那只手腕发出清脆的断裂声，针管脱手。
格林的另一只手同时击中它的头颅——不，那不是头颅，只是头部的位置——那东西像一块被重锤击中的石板一样碎裂开来。
黑色的人影倒地。没有血，只有某种浓稠的、像墨汁一样的液体从碎裂处流出。
剩下的几只同样没有撑过更多的时间。
格林站在房间中央，低头看着那些渐渐消散的黑色残骸。
“看起来有点古怪，但是清理起来并不费劲。”
他走出房间，走廊里的灯没有变化。格林向前走了几步，然后他停下。
因为走廊变了，那些之前还在的墙壁消失了，取而代之的是一扇又一扇门。密密麻麻的，几乎铺满了整个视野。
就像那面满是门的墙一样——但这一次，它们是在走廊的两侧，而且大小看起来好像是一样的。
content_en:
Singing slowly came from deep in the corridor of the mental hospital.
The sound was very old, like an old record played on some kind of gramophone, with a rustling noise, the pitch was high and low, and occasionally out of tune, but it also had a weird melody that made people want to listen. The vocals are a bit muffled, the lyrics are unclear, and only a few fragmentary words can be vaguely discerned.
Green didn't pay attention. He just walked in the corridor and opened one door after another. The numbers on the doors were blurred, and some of the rooms were empty, with only a toppled bed and dusty floors.
Some rooms are filled with old medical records, the paper is yellowed, and the handwriting on it looks like some kind of lost script that cannot be read;
The door to some rooms was blocked by something - like some kind of huge, black block, tightly blocked.
Green didn't push those away, he just kept walking.
After turning a corner, he stopped in front of a door. This one was a little different from the others.
Green pushed open the door. The room was small. There is something mounted on the wall inside - a lever. It's brass-colored, and the handle has been polished and shiny, as if it's been pulled by many people.
Green walked over and looked down at the lever. You can feel that the base of the tie rod is connected to some kind of magical circuit, and those circuits extend into the walls and floors like tree roots, leading to every corner of the entire building.
"It seems to change some of the room structure, but allows the real path to show through."
Green carefully looked at the direction of the circuits. They are intricate, but they do not form a closed loop—that is, they are not traps.
At least it's not the kind of trap that will directly blow up the people in the room to pieces. For Green, it doesn't matter even if it explodes, but it would be terrible if Alice's clue disappears.
Green grasped the lever and pulled it down.
"Click."
The lights went out instantly.
At the same time, there was a rush of footsteps in the corridor outside the room - it sounded like friction, like many pairs of shoe soles moving quickly on the rough ground.
Green released the lever and turned to face the door.
Then those figures poured in, huge black figures, half taller than normal humans. They were wearing white nurses' uniforms, but the white had turned yellow and was stained with dark stains.
They held needles in their hands - not ordinary needles, those needles were as long as arms, and the needle tips glowed ominously in the dark. The face is black and has nothing on it. It is not the same as the pedestrian monster before.
Green moved.
He had no weapon - the broken sword had been completely destroyed before entering the mental hospital. But Green doesn't need weapons now, his hands are weapons.
The first nurse monster rushed over and stabbed his chest with a needle.
Green turned sideways, grabbed the wrist holding the needle with his left hand, and twisted it hard. Click. The wrist made a crisp snapping sound, and the needle fell out of hand.
Green's other hand hit its head simultaneously - no, that wasn't the head, just the position of the head - and the thing shattered like a slab of stone struck by a heavy hammer.
The black figure fell to the ground. There was no blood, just some thick, ink-like liquid flowing from the fracture.
The remaining ones also didn't last much longer.
Green stood in the center of the room, looking down at the black wreckage that was gradually dissipating.
“It looks a little weird, but it’s easy to clean up.”
He walked out of the room and the lights in the corridor did not change. Greene took a few steps forward, then he stopped.
Because the corridor has changed, the walls that existed before disappeared and were replaced by doors one after another. Densely packed, almost covering the entire field of vision.
Just like that wall full of doors - but this time, they're on either side of the hallway and appear to be the same size.
